app.title: Western Flyer - CTD (SBE 19plus V2)
app.summary: The person picks a cruise and one of its stations, then narrows the data to a depth range. They can drop rows flagged for quality and show or hide the surface soak. A cruise summary table and a map give an overview of every cast, and a vertical section shows one chosen variable interpolated along the cruise track, with density contours. For the selected station, they read its vertical profiles side by side and on one multi-axis plot, along with diagnostics computed from the profile: temperature against salinity, density stability with a mixed-layer depth, oxygen utilization and a metabolic index. Finally they look through the binned rows in a table and export the filtered station as a CSV.

task.text: Explore processed instrument casts from a cruise station by station, compute derived water-column diagnostics, and export the filtered profile data.

data.text: Depth-binned vertical profiles of several sensor variables, one profile per station cast, grouped by cruise, with positions, start times and per-bin quality flags.
data.item: a station cast: one vertical profile of binned sensor values from the surface down

stage.text: exploring processed profiler casts after a cruise, before further analysis

mechanism.text: Sidebar selectors for cruise, station, depth range, quality filter and soak toggle drive a single filtered query, and every tab redraws from it. The tabs hold an overview table, a map, an along-track section, profile plots and derived diagnostics. The map marks the selected station among all of them, and the export button saves the same filtered rows.

field.text: CTD vertical profile processing and analysis (EOS-80) in oceanography

workflow.name: inspect measured profiles one location at a time and export the filtered data

steps.here: The dashboard reads the processed cast database. Choosing a cruise reloads its station list, sorted by station number.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A station selector, a depth range slider, a 'Filter QC (Flag < 3)' checkbox and a 'Show Soak Data' toggle narrow the query that every tab uses.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A cruise summary table lists every cast with its position, start time, maximum depth and a 'Health %' bar. A map marks every station, with the selected one highlighted.
A vertical section places all stations along the cumulative distance travelled, interpolates the variable chosen in a selector onto a grid, and overlays density contours and station markers.
The selected station's profiles are drawn as six depth panels sharing one depth axis, and again as one plot with a separate colour-coded axis for each variable. A legend click hides a line.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: From the filtered profile it computes a temperature–salinity plot coloured by depth, a density curve with a mixed-layer-depth line, apparent oxygen utilization against saturation, and a metabolic index with a threshold line.
A paginated table shows the binned rows. 'Export CSV' saves the current station, depth range and filters as CTD_Export.csv.

distinctive: Quality flags and the surface soak are switched in or out as filters, so the person sees how much flagged data affects each profile.
Depth is the shared vertical axis for every profile view and is inverted, so the surface is at the top.
The section's x-axis is great-circle distance accumulated along the stations in time order, so stations appear in the order they were sampled.

Derived quantities come from seawater equations of state rather than simple statistics: oxygen saturation and its deficit, a density-threshold mixed-layer depth, and a temperature-dependent metabolic index.
Each cast carries a percentage of good-quality bins, shown as a progress bar in the overview table.
